eventPage.text: Outdoor Movie Night – Friends of Duboce Park > Feed" href="https://friendsofdubocepark.org/feed/" /> > Comments Feed" href="https://friendsofdubocepark.org/comments/feed/" /> Skip to content Friends of Duboce Park San Francisco Menu About Us Mission Statement President’s Message History of Friends of Duboce Park Membership Info History of Duboce Park About the Harvey Milk Recreation Center Newsletters Events & Activities Events Calendar Monthly Volunteer Days Harvey Milk Courses and Programs Harvey Milk Photo Center Exhibits and Shows World Labyrinth Day Duboce ParkJam Outdoor Movie Night Pumpkin Carving Party 125th Anniversary Celebration 125th Anniversary Merch Rec & Parks Updates Park Maintenance Safety Free WiFi in Duboce Park Contact Location Map Contact Information Home Events & Activities Outdoor Movie Night Outdoor Movie Night Outdoor Movie Night returns to Duboce Park on Saturday, May 30, 2026 with Jurassic Park. The movie will begin at about 8:30 p.m. on the upper lawn. The event is free to attend but donations to Friends of Duboce Park are welcome. Various snacks will be available for purchase (cash preferred). Please remember to pack out your trash and recyclables after the event. Thank you for helping to keep our park clean! The N Judah stops right at Duboce Park and there are many other MUNI lines within a few blocks of the park. For more information or to sponsor, please contact movienight@friendsofdubocepark.org . The next Outdoor Movie Night will return Saturday, September 26, 2026 . Stayed tuned for more updates. Past Movie Nights October 4, 2025 Outdoor Movie Night returned to Duboce Park on Saturday, October 4 with Disney’s Coco . The movie began at 7 p.m. on the upper lawn. September 6, 2024 Sundown Cinema was in Duboce Park on Friday, September 6 for an exclusive showing of San Francisco’s Lost Landscapes: Found Home Movies . Many park regulars thought this was the biggest crowd ever in Duboce Park with attendance estimated at 500 people. SF’s Lost Landscapes is an eclectic montage of lost and rarely-seen film clips showing life, landscapes and labor in San Francisco as captured by amateurs, newsreel cameramen and industrial filmmakers. The footage was carefully curated by Rick Prelinger, a Bay Area guerrilla archivist who collects the home movies showing San Francisco’s people, neighborhoods, infrastructures, and celebrations from the early 20th century through the 1980s. Sundown Cinema was presented by San Francisco Parks Alliance and Alamo Drafthouse Cinema . It is produced by SF Parks Alliance and DoTheBay in partnership with the SF Rec & Park, SF OEWD, Presidio Trust, and Port of San Francisco. May 11, 2024 Outdoor Movie Night returned to Duboce Park on Saturday, May 11 with Rogue One: A Star Wars Story. The movie began at 8 p.m. on the upper lawn with local band Pistachio Fever playing beforehand at 6 p.m. A special thanks to Otra for sponsoring this movie night. May the Fourth (+1 week) Be With You! September 30, 2023 Outdoor Movie Night returned to Duboce Park again this year on Saturday, September 30 with The Super Mario Bros. Movie. The movie began at 7 p.m. on the upper lawn. April 29, 2023 Outdoor Movie Night returned to Duboce Park on Saturday, April 29 with Top Gun: Maverick, starring Tom Cruise. The 2022 action film is a sequel to the 1986 Top Gun with Cruise reprising his starring role as the naval aviator Maverick. It won the Academy Award for Best Sound and was nominated for five other Oscars including Best Picture, Best Achievement in Film Editing, Best Achievement in Music Written for Motion Pictures, Best Achievement in Visual Effects, and Best Adapted Screenplay. Top Gun: Maverick was the highest-grossing film of 2022, grossing $1.487 billion, the highest grossing film of Cruise’s career. The movie began at 8 p.m. on the upper lawn. August 23, 2018 An estimated 700 people attended outdoor movie night in Duboce Park on Thursday, August 23 to see Best in Show, a 2000 mockumentary film that offered a look into the highly competitive and cut-throat world of dog shows through the eyes of a group of ruthless dog owners. The movie won 11 awards, including AFI Movie of the Year and received 14 other nominations in a variety of categories. Fortunately, the weather was mild and there was no wind. The festivities started at 6 p.m. with a dog costume contest, free balloon animals, food trucks, a beer and wine booth, and Duboce Park Café had a snack booth. The movie was part of Sundown Cinema, a series of free movies being shown in four San Francisco parks on Thursdays. Sundown Cinema in Duboce Park was organized by San Francisco Parks Alliance and was hosted by Friends of Duboce Park. Other movies shown in other parks so far are Little Shop of Horrors at Conservatory of Flowers on June 28 and Mrs. Doubtfire in Alamo Square on June 26. The final movie is Grease and will be shown at the Jerry Garcia Amphitheater in McLaren Park on September 28.
